column1: # *** NUNO FERNANDO LERENA'S OWN PAPERS, supplied by David on 13 October 2026 ***
# Eleven items. Seven are published as images on his page and on /family-papers/; the 1971 death-notice photograph, the 1997 letter,
# the family's thank-you card and the tennis-club cutting are NOT, because they name the living or carry a private address. Every person pictured or named in a published image is dead.
# The figures were read at full size on 13 October 2026. 'as written' means as the clerk wrote it.

column4: what it adds, and what it does not

column2: Birth certificate A 042921 (abridged extract), entry 664/24, District Wynberg
column3: Nuno Fernando Lerena, male, born Sixth October 1924 at Wynberg. Race of parents: 'Spanish and European'. Certified 8 September 1954 by the registrar, Cape; fee 2/6.
column4: The birth is now documented at the register, not only at the font: Corpus Christi no. 4540 gave the baptism, this gives the civil entry and the place. It names no parents (an abridged extract), and 'Spanish' is the clerk's race word for Pablo Armando, who was Argentine. THE EXTRACT WAS ISSUED FOUR WEEKS BEFORE HIS THIRTIETH BIRTHDAY, 6 October 1954 - the day the will made the capital payable. That he asked for it to prove his age is a CANDIDATE reading, not shown.

column2: Abridged marriage certificate no. 616593, BMD 163, issued under Act 81 of 1963
column3: Nuno Fernando Lerena, 24, and Catherine Mary Sophia Booyzen, 19, both 'European', married 15 January 1949 at Johannesburg, Transvaal, without ante-nuptial contract; 'Catholic'. Identity-number boxes dashed for both. Office stamp 18-3-1971.
column4: The marriage has a DATE: 15 January 1949, which the archive had only as 'm. Johannesburg'. The ages agree with both birth dates (b. 6 Oct 1924 = 24; b. 25 Mar 1929 = 19). The extract was stamped 18 March 1971, three and a half months before he died - why it was wanted is not known. Place of marriage is Johannesburg, which matters for the 1997 letter below.

column2: Abridged death certificate A 243689, BMD 166, entry 581/71, District Germiston
column3: Nuno Fernando Lerena, white male, died First July 1971 at Germiston, aged 46, born 6.10.1924, married, salesman, pension nil; coronary thrombosis, four hours; Dr Lieberberg. Identity number written 331-406057. Office stamp 2 Sep 1971.
column4: Cause and duration of death, and the doctor, are new. Age, date, occupation and marital status agree with the estate death notice 6746/71. ONE DIGIT DISAGREES: the notice and the 1958 identity card both give 331 406051 W; this handwritten certificate reads 331-406057. Two sources against one, and a clerk's 1 and 7 are easily confused, so 051 stands, but the certificate has not been shown to be the one in error.

column2: Identity card, 'Persoonskaart / Identity Card', S.A. Burger - S.A. Citizen, Pretoria, 1-9-58
column3: Printed LERENA N F, male, no. 331 406051 W, signed by the Director of Census; photograph. Date read as 1 September 1958, day-month-year as on the 22.8.53 deed - the card does not say so.
column4: The number is the same as the one on the 1971 death notice, which is what closes the identification: this is Nuno Fernando, not an N. F. Lerena of somebody else's. The only likeness of him this archive holds. No birth date, birthplace or parent on the card.

column2: Headstone photograph, supplied by David, cemetery not stated
column3: LERENA. Nuno Fernando (Larry) 6.10.1924 - 1.7.1971, with Catherine Tertia 21.5.1952 - 30.9.1999; Catherine Mary Sophia 25.3.1929 - 25.12.2013, with Paul Raymond 11.3.1951 - 24.12.2000. Epitaph: 'Remember friend as you walk by...'
column4: The first sight of the NICKNAME, 'Larry', which the 1971 newspaper notices repeat. Every date agrees with the death certificate and the death notice for Nuno, and with the birth year on the 1949 marriage extract for his wife. One stone carries four people, two of them his children, who died at 49 and 47 - the stone was inscribed after 2013. THE CEMETERY IS NOT ON THE PHOTOGRAPH and has not been established; Johannesburg is the guess, and a guess is all it is.

column2: Photograph of the 1971 death notice, estate MHG 6746/71, supplied again by David on 13 October 2026
column3: 24 Leiden Road, Gerdview, Germiston; 331 406051W; Salesman; place of marriage Johannesburg; parents 'Deceased' and a ditto mark.
column4: Already read on 16 September 2026; this is the image that reading came from, and it confirms the ID number and the Johannesburg marriage. NOT PUBLISHED AS AN IMAGE: it names living children, and this estate names the living and nothing more.

column2: A letter of 21 August 1997 to 'Paul' (Nuno's son Paul Raymond Lerena, who died in 2000), from Gavin Knott, writing with his wife Diana
column3: (1) His grandmother had a house in Newlands, Cape Town, where 'your grandfather boarded there for longer than I can remember'. (2) His aunt, Rose Theys, and Pablo 'used to attend all racing functions together'. (3) Nuno and 'Cardo' lived there while at Marist Brothers College, Rondebosch; Nuno was then sent to live with the writer's family at Stellenbosch for about two years, attending the local boys' high school. (4) After school Nuno 'joined the Air Force and served in the Western Desert'; 'on his return to Cape Town he married and then moved to Johannesburg'. (5) At Pablo's death the writer was to keep 'a watching brief on the stables'; Peter Kannemeyer and Alan Higgens were apprentices there. (6) Papers found among his aunt's things were enclosed, with a photograph of a couple he could not name.
column4: THE FIRST THING IN THIS ARCHIVE THAT EXPLAINS WHY ROSE THEYS, 'NO RELATION' IN THE 1950 DISTRIBUTION ACCOUNT, SHARED PABLO'S ADDRESS: she was his landlady's daughter, on this account - 'my aunt', 'my grandmother's house' - which makes Gavin Knott her nephew and the Newlands house hers before it was Pablo's. That reading is INFERRED from the letter, not stated in it. Points (3) fits the 1936 Marist testimonials and the Rondebosch placement exactly, and puts Ricardo ('Cardo') in the same school and house. Point (4) has a conflict: he married at JOHANNESBURG in January 1949, not after returning to Cape Town, so the order or the place is wrong in a 1997 memory; the certificate governs. 'Western Desert' is a recollection of a recollection - Nuno was 18 in 1942 - and no service record has been seen, though a 1971 notice from '12th Squadron, S.A.A.F.' (below) supports the Air Force. NOT PUBLISHED AS AN IMAGE: it carries a private address.

column2: Printed wedding invitation, English and Afrikaans, St Joseph's Catholic Church, Mayfair
column3: Catherine, second eldest daughter of the late Mr and Mrs G. Booyzen (Brakpan), to Nuno, youngest son of Mr and the late Mrs R. Lerena (Mayfair), Saturday 15 January 1949 at 3.45 p.m.; no reception; telegrams to 45 Railway Street, Mayfair.
column4: THE DATE, THE CHURCH AND THE PARENTAGE IN HIS OWN FAMILY'S WORDS. 15 January 1949 was a Saturday, as printed. 'The late Mrs R. Lerena' is Mary Septima, dead since 1935, and 'Mr R. Lerena' is Pablo Armando ('Robert'), alive and named as his father fourteen months before he died. 'Youngest son' is right: Roque 1905, Ricardo 1920, Nuno 1924. It puts Nuno at MAYFAIR before the marriage - the suburb where Roque had married in 1936 at the same church - which fits a family moving north to Johannesburg together rather than singly. It does not say when he left Cape Town.

column2: Newspaper 'Deaths' notice, July 1971: 'LERENA. - Larry. Finally into wide, blue yonder. Deepest sympathy to family. Remembered by 12th Squadron, S.A.A.F. Friend.' (-84290)
column3: Signed as from the 12th Squadron, S.A.A.F. The newspaper and date are not on the cutting.
column4: THE FIRST DOCUMENT THAT SUPPORTS HIS AIR-FORCE SERVICE, written by somebody else in 1971. It names a unit, 12 Squadron, which flew in the Western Desert in the early 1940s as bombers (from general history, not from any record seen here). It does not give his service, rank, dates or number, and 'Remembered by' could be a squadron association writing for a former member of it. 'Larry' is the nickname also on the headstone. It moves the 1997 letter's 'Air Force' from a recollection to a recollection with a second witness; it does not yet show he was at the Western Desert.
column5: DOCUMENTED, AS TO THE NOTICE; SERVICE NOT YET SHOWN

column3: 'The family of the late Larry Lerena thank you for your kind thoughts ... from Cathy and family', with the address 24 Leiden STREET, Gerdview, Germiston.
column4: The family's own address, written 'Street' where the estate death notice has 'Leiden Road' - the same house, a different word for it; Gerdview is the township the two land records place him in. Not published because it carries the family's home address and 'and family'.

column2: Newspaper cutting, July 1971: 'Eastleigh tennis chief dies suddenly at 46' (not published)
column3: Larry Lerena, chairman and a founder member of Eastleigh Tennis Club, died suddenly at his home in Germiston 'on Thursday last week' (1 July 1971 was a Thursday). He started the club at St Joseph's Convent in 1959, was made an honorary life member when ill-health forced him to give up tennis, and won three courts and R5,000 for a clubhouse from the City Council. Born at Cape Town 6 October 1924. Survived by his wife, five children, a son-in-law and a granddaughter.
column4: A life after 1949: a community role in Germiston, a Catholic convent connection (consistent with the Catholic marriage and the Marist schooling), and ill-health 'during the past three years' before a coronary death. The five children agree in number with the 1971 death notice. NOT PUBLISHED, and the survivors are not named here: it names living people.
